summary: Cheryl A. Crowley is a Japanology scholar who studied under William R. LaFleur, Philip B. Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.

Chi Chen Ho, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, earned a PhD from UCLA in 2010 under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr. and studied under traditional teacher Hsuan Hua. Ho also served as a UCLA teaching assistant.

Chi-chiang Huang, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology, completed a PhD at the University of Arizona in 1986 under doctoral supervisor Jing-shen Tao and also studied under Robert M. Gimello.

Chi-wah Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD from UCLA in 1993, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman. Chan also served as a teaching assistant at CUHK.
Chie Ikeya is a historian and archaeologist who completed a PhD at Cornell University in 2006 under the direction of David K. Wyatt.

Chien Y. Hsu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura (until 2011) and James B. Apple (attested 2013), as well as traditional teacher Zhenhua (attested 2013).

Chien-hsing Ho is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Ho served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and held a post at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).

Chih-mien Adrian Tseng works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Tseng earned a PhD from McMaster University under James A. Benn, Nobuyoshi Yamabe, and Canshan Cheng, and was an Assistant Professor at Fo Guang University (attested 2016).

Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1907–1910) and the University of Tokyo. He was appointed the first professor at Keijo Imperial University in 1927 and also held a post at Yamaguchi University.

Chikafumi Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar with a master's from the University of British Columbia and a PhD from the University of Calgary. Supervised by Leslie S. Kawamura and Ashok Aklujkar, Watanabe also studied under Karin Preisendanz and others.
Chiko Corona is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Kenkō Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura (attested 2010).
Chikyo Yamamoto (1913–1999) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor (attested 1970) and part-time lecturer (attested 1980) at Koyasan University.

Ching-mei Shyu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned an MA at the University of Hawaii under Jan Nattier and a PhD at Cornell University (2008) supervised by Daniel Boucher, Hubert Durt, and Jane-Marie Law.
Chishō Namai (born 1947) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who served as a professor (attested 1996) and later president (attested 2008) at Koyasan University.

Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed a degree at Kyoto University in 1968. He was an assistant professor at Hanazono University (1979–1983) and a professor at Tokoha University (attested 1989).

Chizuko Yoshimizu is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. After studying at the University of Tokyo and the University of Vienna, she was a research assistant at Naritasan Institute (1991) and professor at the University of Tsukuba (2015).
Chlodwig H. Werba is an Indology and linguistics scholar who held posts as a professor at the University of Vienna, attested between 1997 and 2022. He also taught Vitus Angermeier.
Chogye Shabdrung (born 1981) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sakya College in 2003 under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso.

Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) was the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Nalendra Monastery (1928), working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Tsechok and the 13th Dalai Lama, and taught scholars including Cyrus Stearns and David P. Jackson.

Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche (born 1951) is a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology scholar who founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and taught James B. Apple.
